subject: pathology
title: Achalasia, Barrett Oesophagus, Oesophageal Cancers, and Mallory-Weiss Tears

steps.tx: Achalasia destroys inhibitory myenteric neurons so the lower oesophageal sphincter fails to relax and aperistalsis fills a dilating oesophagus with retained food, regurgitation, weight loss, and bird beak barium tapering. The relaxation failure is **achalasia of the cardia**. Regurgitation worsens lying flat, and nocturnal aspiration cough often appears before major weight loss develops.
steps.say: Dysphagia for solids and liquids together with bird beak barium means achalasia, not stricture.

vis.caption: Achalasia bird beak tapering at the gastro-oesophageal junction.

steps.tx: Manometry confirms achalasia subtypes by pressurisation patterns guiding Heller myotomy, pneumatic dilation, or peroral endoscopic myotomy, while longstanding disease raises squamous cancer risk modestly. Subtype guided therapy is **manometric achalasia subtyping (Chicago classification)**. Type two achalasia, with panesophageal pressurisation, responds best to pneumatic dilation among the three subtypes.
steps.say: Manometry subtypes achalasia and chooses among myotomy, dilation, and POEM more honestly than symptoms.

steps.tx: Barrett oesophagus replaces reflux burnt squamous epithelium with intestinal metaplasia bearing goblet cells, the premalignant soil from which oesophageal adenocarcinoma rises through dysplasia grades. That metaplastic replacement is **Barrett oesophagus with intestinal metaplasia**. Endoscopy must exclude pseudoachalasia from a cardia tumour before any myotomy or dilation is planned.
steps.say: Goblet cells above the junction mean Barrett oesophagus; dysplasia grade schedules its surveillance or ablation.

vis.caption: Barrett oesophagus to adenocarcinoma sequence through dysplasia.

steps.tx: Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma follows alcohol, tobacco, hot beverages, achalasia, and nutritional insults in upper and middle thirds, while adenocarcinoma follows reflux, Barrett change, and obesity in the lower third. Geography separates them: **oesophageal cancer by site and cause**. Plummer-Vinson syndrome links iron deficiency, dysphagia and postcricoid webs to squamous carcinoma risk.
steps.say: Upper and middle thirds squamous from smoke and drink; lower third adeno from reflux and Barrett change.

steps.tx: Dysphagia progressing from solids to liquids with weight loss in an older smoker is oesophageal cancer until endoscopy acquits, because benign strictures usually spare weight and progress slower. That alarm rule is **progressive dysphagia, exclude oesophageal malignancy**. Liquids sticking from the very first swallow suggests a motility disorder rather than a fixed stricture.
steps.say: Solids then liquids plus weight loss earns urgent endoscopy; oesophageal cancer hides behind stricture stories.

steps.tx: Mallory-Weiss tears split gastro-oesophageal junction mucosa longitudinally after forceful retching, classically alcoholic binges, bleeding briskly yet usually stopping spontaneously with endoscopic therapy in reserve. The retching tear is the **Mallory-Weiss mucosal laceration**. Most tears settle with acid suppression alone, reserving clips or thermal therapy for continuing haemorrhage.
steps.say: Retch first, bleed second: Mallory-Weiss tears follow vomiting force at the cardia.

steps.tx: Eosinophilic oesophagitis rings and furrows young atopic food impaction patients, requiring biopsies despite normal looking mucosa and dietary or topical steroid therapy. The allergic ringed oesophagus is **eosinophilic oesophagitis of atopic patients**. Fifteen or more eosinophils per high power field on oesophageal biopsy support the diagnosis.
steps.say: Food impaction in a young atopic man means eosinophilic oesophagitis; biopsy even normal looking mucosa.

steps.tx: Corrosive ingestion, radiation, and infections complete benign stricture differentials whose dilatation and cause therapy contrast sharply with malignant obstruction stenting and oncology. Cause first remains **benign versus malignant oesophageal stricture separation**. Alkali ingestion injures the oesophagus by liquefactive necrosis, deeper than most acid burns produce.
steps.say: Dilate benign strictures, stent or treat malignant ones; biopsy decides which road a stricture travels.
